patients.summary: Administrative assistant with childhood rheumatic fever and rheumatic mitral stenosis, unfollowed for years, who joins in 2020 on a thiazide. Cardiology finds severe mitral stenosis with heart failure in 2022 and paroxysmal AF on Holter (warfarin), then pulmonary hypertension in 2024; after her last practice visit in July 2024 she has an ED visit and admission for decompensated heart failure in 2026 and a balloon valvotomy, known to the practice only through late records and her messages.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
40-year-old woman new to the practice, transferring from another primary care office.

HPI: Had rheumatic fever as a child. Was told around high school that one of her heart valves (mitral) was narrowed from it. Saw a heart doctor a few times back then, nothing for many years since. During her last pregnancy in 2017 she got short of breath and puffy; the OB team put her on a diuretic and told her to cut salt. Her prior PCP kept her on HCTZ 25 with potassium afterward. Today she feels fine. Works full time as an administrative assistant, climbs the stairs at work without stopping. No chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, leg swelling, fainting.

PMH: rheumatic fever in childhood, rheumatic mitral valve disease.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 8.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FH: mother had rheumatic fever. Father has type 2 diabetes. A maternal uncle had an ischemic stroke at 65.
SH: never smoker, does not drink, no drug use. Administrative assistant.

Exam: well appearing, NAD. BP 116/74. Neck: no JVD. Heart: regular rhythm; low apical diastolic murmur, otherwise normal sounds. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Ext: no edema. Skin intact.

A/P:
1. Rheumatic heart disease, mitral valve: known since adolescence, never re-imaged as an adult that she knows of. She has no symptoms on the thiazide. Recommended she get back in with cardiology for an echo and baseline; referral placed. She is agreeable though busy with work.
2. Diuretic: continue HCTZ 25 and KCl 20. CMP today.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c (father diabetic), TSH; one-time HIV and hep C screens, consented. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap due per her history, will do at the physical in spring. Flu shot next month, nurse visit.
4. Prior records requested.

Return for a physical in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jessenia, all of your blood work from last week looks good. Kidney function, sodium and potassium are normal on the water pill. Blood counts, sugar (A1c), thyroid and cholesterol are all in a healthy range. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Please keep the cardiology appointment on your list when they call you.

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: winded with exertion, tired.

HPI: Over roughly the past several months she has had to stop halfway up the stairs at work and gets breathless with housework, which she never used to. Tired by mid-afternoon. Now and then feels her heart flutter for a few minutes. Ankles swell toward evening and are down by morning. Denies chest pain, cough, or needing to sleep propped up. No fever. Meds unchanged, takes them daily.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable at rest, speaking in full sentences. No JVD. Heart: regular today, loud first sound, low rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear to auscultation today. Trace to mild ankle edema both sides.

A/P:
1. Exertional dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations and edema in a patient with rheumatic mitral valve disease: concerning for progression of the stenosis. She agrees to cardiology now. Referral placed as urgent; asked them for the earliest new-patient slot. Echo will come through them.
2. Checking CBC, BMP and TSH for other causes of fatigue.
3. Continue HCTZ and KCl, keep salt down. ED precautions reviewed.
Follow up after cardiology.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count, thyroid and kidney/electrolyte tests are normal, so anemia and thyroid trouble are not the reason for the tiredness. Cardiology has you on October 11 - please keep that appointment.

conditions.label: Rheumatic heart failure
conditions.note: chronic heart failure from mitral stenosis, LVEF 60%

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 50 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet
medications.reason: heart rate control in mitral stenosis

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 92. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST-segment or T-wave changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm, 92 bpm. No acute ST changes.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Heart size within normal limits. Mild pulmonary vascular congestion. No pleural effusion, no focal consolidation, no pneumothorax. Bones unremarkable.

Complete 2D, M-mode and Doppler study. Mitral valve: rheumatic appearance with commissural fusion and diastolic doming of the anterior leaflet. Mitral valve area 1.1 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 10 mmHg at a heart rate of 92. Left atrium enlarged, LA volume index 52 mL/m2. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness, LVEF 60%, no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal size and function. Estimated PA systolic pressure 38 mmHg. Aortic, tricuspid and pulmonic valves without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis (MVA 1.1 cm2, mean gradient 10 mmHg). Enlarged left atrium. Normal LV function, LVEF 60%. Estimated PASP 38 mmHg.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - consultation letter
Visit date: 10/11/2022
Referred by: primary care
Reason: rheumatic mitral valve disease with worsening exertional symptoms

Thank you for asking us to see this 42-year-old woman. She had rheumatic fever as a child and was told of a mitral valve problem in her teens, but has not been followed by cardiology in many years. Over several months she has become short of breath with stairs and household chores, tires easily, has occasional palpitations and notices her legs swell late in the day. No chest pain, cough or orthopnea.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA
PSH: tonsillectomy age 8.
Family: mother with rheumatic fever; father with type 2 diabetes; maternal uncle with stroke at 65.
Social: administrative assistant, never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: HR 92, BP 118/72. Loud S1. Low-pitched rumbling diastolic murmur at the apex, best with the bell with the patient turned onto her left side. Fine crackles at both bases. Mild ankle edema bilaterally. No JVD.

ECG: sinus rhythm 92, no ST changes.
Chest x-ray: mild pulmonary vascular congestion.
Echo today: rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion and doming; MVA 1.1 cm2 by planimetry, mean gradient 10 mmHg at HR 92; LA enlarged (LAVI 52 mL/m2); LVEF 60%; RV normal; PASP estimated 38 mmHg.

Impression:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis.
2. Chronic heart failure due to mitral stenosis, LV function preserved.
3. Palpitations, rhythm not yet defined.

Plan:
- Start metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily to slow the heart rate and lengthen diastolic filling.
- Continue hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and KCl 20 mEq; 2 g sodium diet.
- 48-hour Holter to look for atrial fibrillation.
- Return after the Holter.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth daily in the evening or as directed by the anticoagulation clinic; goal INR 2.0-3.0
medications.reason: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rheumatic mitral stenosis

reports.text: 48-hour ambulatory ECG, 10/18/2022 to 10/20/2022. Predominant rhythm sinus, mean heart rate 88. Three episodes of atrial fibrillation, longest 3 hours 10 minutes; AF burden 6%. Ventricular rate during AF up to 138. Patient-triggered events for palpitations correspond to atrial fibrillation. No pauses, no sustained ventricular arrhythmia.
reports.conclusion: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, burden 6%, with symptomatic episodes.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group - follow-up letter (sent at your request)
Visit date: 11/08/2022

Returns to review her Holter. Tolerating metoprolol, palpitations less frequent. Holter 10/18-10/20: mostly sinus rhythm, mean HR 88, three runs of atrial fibrillation up to 3 h 10 min (burden 6%), rates to 138 in AF, matching her symptom diary.

Impression: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with severe rheumatic mitral stenosis. Anticoagulation is indicated regardless of risk score in this setting; a DOAC is not appropriate with rheumatic mitral stenosis.

Plan: start warfarin 5 mg daily, dose adjusted to INR 2.0-3.0, managed by our anticoagulation clinic (first INR in one week). Continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and KCl 20 mEq. Return in 6 months or sooner for symptoms.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back after cardiology. The October consult letter is here (severe rheumatic MS, MVA 1.1 cm2, EF 60%, metoprolol started). She tells me the heart monitor showed atrial fibrillation coming and going and that two weeks ago cardiology started warfarin; their anticoagulation clinic is checking her INR weekly for now. Pharmacy fill history confirms warfarin 5 mg filled 11/8. We do not have that letter or the Holter report yet. Breathing a little better on the metoprolol, still winded on the stairs. Fewer flutters. Ankles less swollen.

Meds now: HCTZ 25 daily, KCl ER 20 mEq daily, metoprolol succinate 50 daily, warfarin 5 mg daily per anticoag clinic.

O: Vitals as charted. Regular rhythm today. Loud S1, apical diastolic rumble. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis with chronic heart failure: followed by cardiology. Continue meds and low-salt diet.
2. Paroxysmal AF on warfarin (per patient and pharmacy): will request the cardiology note and Holter. Warfarin teaching: bleeding signs, keep vitamin K foods steady, no ibuprofen or naproxen, acetaminophen is fine, tell us before any new medicine or antibiotic. Warfarin can harm a pregnancy - she is not planning one and understands to tell us right away if that changes.
3. Long-term anticoagulant use added to problem list.
4. BMP and CBC today.
Follow up in 4 months for her physical.

reports.text: Comparison 10/2022. Rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion. Mitral valve area 0.9 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 13 mmHg at a heart rate of 104. LA volume index 58 mL/m2. LV normal size, LVEF 60%. Right ventricle mildly dilated with preserved systolic function. Estimated PA systolic pressure 56 mmHg. No pericardial effusion.

Outside cardiology group - follow-up note (faxed on request)
Visit date: 04/15/2024

She is back for her rheumatic mitral stenosis, first seen here in October 2022 for progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue. Her exertional breathlessness and tiredness have crept up over the last several years, and she now needs extra pillows at night. She reports taking hydrochlorothiazide every day as directed.

Echo: MVA 0.9 cm2, mean gradient 13 mmHg at HR 104, LAVI 58 mL/m2, LVEF 60%, RV mildly dilated with normal function, PASP 56 mmHg.

Impression:
1. Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, progressing.
2. Pulmonary hypertension due to mitral stenosis (WHO group 2).
3. Chronic heart failure, new orthopnea.
4. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin.

Plan: no medication changes today. Continue sodium restriction. Follow up in cardiology.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital emergency department - physician record (received by fax 4/21/2026)
Date of service: 3/31/2026

CC: short of breath, heart racing, cough.

HPI: 45-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and pulmonary hypertension followed by cardiology, brought in after a few hours of rapidly increasing breathlessness with palpitations and a cough that kept getting worse.

PMH: rheumatic fever in childhood; rheumatic mitral stenosis; pulmonary hypertension; chronic heart failure; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
PSH: tonsillectomy at 8.
Home meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2-3), potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother rheumatic fever; father type 2 diabetes; maternal uncle stroke at 65.
SH: administrative assistant; never smoker; no alcohol.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 120 and irregularly irregular, RR 22, SpO2 92% on room air. Diastolic rumble at the apex, heard best in left lateral decubitus. Crackles at both bases.

ECG: atrial fibrillation, rapid rate, no ST changes.
CXR: left atrial enlargement, elevated left mainstem bronchus, interstitial edema.
Labs: NT-proBNP 2860 pg/mL; hs-troponin I 9 ng/L; INR 2.4; Na 137, K 3.7, Cr 0.84; Hgb 12.4, WBC 7.6.

ED course: oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula with SpO2 to 96%. Furosemide 40 mg IV. Metoprolol tartrate 5 mg IV twice for rate control. Warfarin therapeutic, held tonight pending inpatient team.

Impression: acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema; atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; severe rheumatic mitral stenosis.
Disposition: admitted to cardiology telemetry.

events.reason: acute decompensated heart failure, atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response

reports.text: Comparison 04/2024. Rheumatic mitral valve with commissural fusion. Mitral valve area 0.8 cm2 by planimetry. Mean transmitral gradient 14 mmHg at a heart rate of 78, sinus rhythm. LVEF 60%. Estimated PA systolic pressure 62 mmHg. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, MVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg. Estimated PASP 62 mmHg. LVEF 60%.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Hospital discharge summary (received 8/11/2026 after patient request)
Admitted 3/31/2026, discharged 4/3/2026. Service: inpatient cardiology.

Principal diagnosis: acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema.
Secondary: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; severe rheumatic mitral stenosis; pulmonary hypertension due to mitral stenosis.

Course: Admitted from the ED after IV furosemide and IV metoprolol. Diuresed with IV furosemide with steady improvement in breathing; off oxygen by day 2. Converted on her own to sinus rhythm on 4/1. Warfarin resumed, INR stayed therapeutic. Echo 4/1: MVA 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg at HR 78, PASP 62 mmHg, LVEF 60%.

Discharge medications:
- Furosemide 40 mg by mouth daily (NEW)
- Metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily (INCREASED from 50 mg)
- Warfarin 5 mg daily, INR goal 2-3 (continue; anticoagulation clinic)
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq daily (continue)
- Hydrochlorothiazide: STOPPED
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: referred to the structural heart program for evaluation for percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy; INR check within a week; primary care follow-up in 1 to 2 weeks.

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacist called: patient filled new furosemide 40 mg daily and metoprolol succinate 100 mg from a hospital discharge on 4/3, and an auto-refill for HCTZ 25 (our Rx) is also queued. Asked whether HCTZ should still be filled. Called pt - she says the hospital told her to stop HCTZ. Told pharmacy to cancel the HCTZ refill. We have no hospital records; requested discharge summary and ED record from the hospital. PCP aware.

documents.title: was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to tell you I was in the hospital at the end of March for 3 days, fluid in my lungs and my heart went into the fast irregular rhythm. They gave me a different water pill and a higher metoprolol and stopped the hydrochlorothiazide. Now they want me to see a valve team about fixing the valve with a balloon. I'm feeling much better.

documents.title: RE: was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, and I'm glad you are feeling better. We have asked the hospital for your records. Please book a visit with me in the next week or two so we can go over your medicines and check your blood work - the front desk can find you a time.

documents.title: Hospital ED record received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hospital sent the 3/31/2026 ED record only; discharge summary not included. Scanned. Second request sent for the discharge summary. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Structural Heart Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Structural heart program - consultation letter
Visit date: 5/19/2026

46-year-old woman with severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, pulmonary hypertension and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hospitalized 3/31-4/3/2026 for decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema and AF with rapid rates. Since discharge her breathing is better: she walks a block and takes stairs slowly. Sinus rhythm today.

Meds: furosemide 40 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily, warfarin 5 mg daily (INR 2-3), potassium chloride 20 mEq daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Review of echoes 2022, 2024 and 4/2026: progressive severe rheumatic MS, MVA now 0.8 cm2, mean gradient 14 mmHg, PASP 62 mmHg, LVEF 60%. Valve anatomy suitable for a balloon approach.

Recommendation: percutaneous balloon mitral valvotomy, preceded by a transesophageal echo to exclude left atrial thrombus. Continue warfarin and the current regimen. Our office will schedule.

Thank you for allowing us to share in her care.

documents.title: valve procedure done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doctor, I had the balloon procedure on my valve last Tuesday, July 21. Went home the next day. I can already breathe easier walking. They said they will send you the report. I still need to make my appointment with you, sorry.

documents.title: RE: valve procedure done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news. We have not received the report yet and will ask for it. Please do come in when you can - I would like to see you and catch up on everything since 2024.
